checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skeletal mount clearly displays the characteristic three-horn configuration: two large brow horns and one smaller nasal horn. The structure matches the anatomical description of a Triceratops skull.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image shows a fossilized skeleton. The 'beak' described in the taxonomy refers to the keratinous rhamphotheca which does not preserve in fossils. checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is quadrupedal with columnar, elephant-like limbs.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Enormous bony frill (neck shield) extending posteriorly from the skull, with width dramatically exceeding the skull itself.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The parietal-squamosal frill is clearly visible, extending wide behind the skull. Its width exceeds the facial portion of the skull, matching the diagnostic criteria.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Frill is solid bone with a smooth outer surface and possible epoccipital (marginal) bumps.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The frill appears solid (non-fenestrated). The texture is consistent with fossilized bone. Marginal epoccipitals are visible along the edge of the frill.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is inferred to have been covered in large, hexagonal scales with possible quill-like structures along the back and tail.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: This is a skeletal mount; no skin, scales, or soft tissue impressions are visible. This checkpoint is impossible to verify on this specific image subject.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Comparing the visible forelimb assembly to the hindlimb assembly, the forelimbs are noticeably shorter, resulting in the characteristic downward slope of the dorsal vertebrae towards the neck.
The caudal vertebrae are visible and appear robust and relatively short compared to the body length, consistent with ceratopsian anatomy.
